hook.line: Sometimes "no" is not enough and you need to close the door and lock it. *Ni aunque* takes the best offer anyone could make and refuses that too.
hook.es: No vuelvo ni aunque me paguen.
hook.en: I'm not going back, not even if they pay me.

rule:
*Ni aunque* means "not even if". You name the best offer and still say no.

Two moods, as in *si* sentences you already know:

A real possibility: present subjunctive. *No vuelvo ni aunque me paguen.* The refusal is in the present.

An imaginary one: imperfect subjunctive, then the conditional. *Ni aunque me pagaran el doble volvería.* Here the reply is *volvería*, not *vuelvo*.

*Ni siquiera si* does the same job: *ni siquiera si me pagaran el doble*.

The *ni* can start the sentence or sit in the middle. Either way it makes the refusal absolute.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an emphatic concessive clause: *ni aunque* is a negative *aunque* with a subjunctive.

readAndPick.es: No vuelvo ni aunque me paguen.
options: I'm not going back, not even if they pay me.
I'm not going back because they pay me.
I'm not going back unless they pay me.

readAndPick.es: Ni aunque me lo pidiera de rodillas lo perdonaría.
options: I forgave him when he begged me on his knees.
I wouldn't forgive him even if he begged me on his knees.
I would forgive him if he begged me on his knees.

readAndPick.es: No firmo ni aunque me lo pidan de rodillas.
options: I'll sign if they beg me on their knees.
I signed because they begged me on their knees.
I'm not signing, not even if they beg me on their knees.

readAndPick.es: Ni siquiera si me pagaran el doble volvería.
options: I wouldn't go back even if they paid me double.
I would go back if they paid me double.
I didn't go back, though they paid me double.

readAndPick.es: No me voy ni aunque me echen.
options: I'm leaving, since they are throwing me out.
I'm not leaving, not even if they throw me out.
I'll leave if they throw me out.

readAndPick.es: Ni aunque me regalaran el carro lo manejaría.
options: They gave me the car and I drive it.
I would drive the car if they gave it to me.
I wouldn't drive that car even if they gave it to me.

readAndPick.es: Ni aunque llueva me quedo en casa.
options: I'm not staying home, not even if it rains.
I'm staying home because it is raining.
I'll stay home if it rains.

readAndPick.es: Ni aunque me pidiera perdón lo perdonaría.
options: He asked me to forgive him and I did.
I wouldn't forgive him even if he apologised.
I'll forgive him as soon as he apologises.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *paguen* or *pagan* and type the whole sentence: *No vuelvo ni aunque me ___.*
yourTurn.answer: No vuelvo ni aunque me paguen.
yourTurn.why: After *ni aunque*, a real possibility takes the subjunctive: *paguen*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm not leaving, not even if they throw me out.
yourTurn.answer: No me voy ni aunque me echen.
accept: Ni aunque me echen me voy.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm not signing, not even if they beg me on their knees.
yourTurn.answer: No firmo ni aunque me lo pidan de rodillas.
accept: Ni aunque me lo pidan de rodillas firmo.
yourTurn.why: The offer goes in the subjunctive: *pidan*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm not staying home, not even if it rains.
yourTurn.answer: Ni aunque llueva me quedo en casa.
accept: No me quedo en casa ni aunque llueva.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it imaginary: *No vuelvo ni aunque me paguen.* Say: I wouldn't go back even if they paid me double.
yourTurn.answer: Ni aunque me pagaran el doble volvería.
accept: No volvería ni aunque me pagaran el doble.
yourTurn.why: Imaginary means imperfect subjunctive, then the conditional *volvería*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I wouldn't drive that car even if they gave it to me.
yourTurn.answer: Ni aunque me regalaran el carro lo manejaría.
accept: No manejaría el carro ni aunque me lo regalaran.
yourTurn.why: *Regalaran* for the imaginary offer, *manejaría* for the refusal.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I wouldn't forgive him even if he apologised.
yourTurn.answer: Ni aunque me pidiera perdón lo perdonaría.
accept: No lo perdonaría ni aunque me pidiera perdón.

pitfalls.wrong: No vuelvo ni aunque me pagan.
pitfalls.right: No vuelvo ni aunque me paguen.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A possible offer after *ni aunque* takes the subjunctive.

pitfalls.wrong: Ni aunque me pagaran el doble vuelvo.
pitfalls.right: Ni aunque me pagaran el doble volvería.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After an imaginary offer, the refusal is in the conditional.
Almost. *Aunque* needs a conjugated verb, not the infinitive.

personal: Think of one thing you refuse to do, whatever the reward, and say it with *ni aunque*.
